# `test/fixtures/`

Frozen reference data and intermediate JSON used by reproducibility /
regression tests. Files here are NOT used by the production code path —
they exist purely to compare a freshly computed result against a
known-good baseline.

## `boxcrete_data_pre_v5.csv`

A frozen byte-for-byte snapshot of `data/boxcrete_data.csv` as it stood
at the V2-merge tip (`73cff6b21e11`, "Merge pull request #26 from
facebookresearch/v2-strength-gp"). Schema and content:

  * 727 rows, 149 unique `Mix_<int>` mix names.
  * 2-class `Material Source ∈ {0, 1}` where the semantic is
    `0 = Mortar ∪ Set 2 Concrete`, `1 = Set 3 Concrete` — the silently
    pooled labelling that the v5 three-class merge replaces (see
    `docs/materials_background.md` for the chemistry-source rationale).
  * Includes the 12 corruption-collision mixes (`Mix_126..Mix_137`)
    where each `Mix_<int>` name covers two physically distinct
    compositions (the v5 merger splits these into 24 distinct canonical
    `C<int>` names).
  * Includes the 15 strength-less mortars (`Mix_60..Mix_74`) that the
    v5 merger drops as useless for GP fitting.

### Why a fixture rather than a tracked alternative dataset?

Keeping a second production-style data file at the top level
(`data/boxcrete_data_pre_v5.csv`, say) invites confusion ("which one is
canonical?"). A fixture under `test/fixtures/` is unambiguously labelled
as reproducibility / regression material. The alternative — relying on
`sl cat -r 73cff6b21e11 data/boxcrete_data.csv` at use-time — would tie
the consumer to a specific commit hash and break for anyone cloning the
repo at a later point.

### Consumers

  * `experiments/model_variant_study.py::v2_baseline` (Stage-0 ablation
    variant of the 3-class+LogNormal study; see
    `experiments/THREE_CLASS_AND_PRIOR_BENCHMARK.md`). Reading from this
    fixture lets the binary-vs-ternary comparison be reproducible after
    `data/boxcrete_data.csv` has been overwritten with v5 content in
    Commit 2 of the materials-classes-and-lengthscale-prior stack.
  * `scripts/test_merge_invariants.py` (sanity check that the fixture
    column schema matches the freshly-merged v5 dataset).
  * `scripts/merge_three_class_data.py` (idempotent re-derivation: if
    the fixture is missing on first run, the merger snapshots the
    current `data/boxcrete_data.csv` to this path before overwriting
    it).

### Maintenance

This fixture is NOT regenerated by any pipeline. It is a permanent,
frozen artifact. If the V2-merge-tip dataset changes (which would be
unusual — that commit is the `main`-branch tip at the time of the
three-class merge), update the fixture by copying the new pre-v5
content here and bumping the row count constant in
`scripts/test_merge_invariants.py::fixture_row_count_pre_v5`.

### `feature_parity_fixture.json`

Snapshot of the V2 feature pipeline's intermediate tensors (raw input
columns + engineered features after `AppendDerivedFeatures`) used by
`test/test_feature_parity_pre_v2.py` to verify the V2 split into
`boxcrete.features` preserved exact numeric agreement with the prior
single-module implementation. See the V2 merge PR (#26) for context.
Regenerate with `python experiments/regenerate_feature_parity_fixture.py`.
